 Actor Ko Kyung-pyo caught drunk driving after truck crash
 Published : Nov. 14, 2026 - 11:05:13
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Choi Jae-hee 
Chasing the Korean context AI can’t code
 Subscribe + 
 Actor Ko Kyung-pyo (CL&Company) 
 Actor Ko Kyung-pyo is under police investigation for drunk driving after crashing his car into a street-cleaning truck in Seoul early Saturday.
 The collision occurred at around 3:30 a.m. in Donggyo-dong, Mapo-gu, while Ko was driving his car, news reports said.
 Police officers dispatched to the scene administered a breathalyzer test, which showed that Ko's blood alcohol concentration exceeded the legal threshold for license revocation.
 Under South Korean law, drivers with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or higher face license revocation. Ko's exact blood alcohol level has not been disclosed.
 Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash, including why Ko got behind the wheel after drinking. It remains unclear whether anyone was injured.
 Ko's agency, CL&Company, issued an apology on his behalf, saying he had acknowledged his wrongdoing.
 "We sincerely apologize to those affected by Ko Kyung-pyo's drunk-driving accident. We also deeply regret the disappointment and concern caused to all those who have placed their trust in him and supported him," the agency said in a statement.
 Ko, 36, launched his acting career in 2010 with the KBS drama "Jungle Fish 2" and gained wider recognition for playing Sun-woo in tvN's popular series "Reply 1988."
 He has since appeared in a number of television productions, including "Don't Dare to Dream," "Chicago Typewriter" and "Love in Contract."
 The actor is scheduled to feature in the second season of tvN's variety show "Bogum Magical," due to premiere in November, as well as Tving's "The Great Escape: Urban Ghost Stories," slated for release in December.
